maria (Customer Success): FYI BrightCart hit repeated 429s this morning around 08:12 PT. They say their Dedicated pool never scaled above the minReplicas. Can someone triage?

lina (Support): Oof. Any immediate repro steps from the customer?

maria (Customer Success): They said a traffic spike ~2x baseline for ~3m. App logs show queued requests then 429s. They shared a condensed timeline and k8s events.

lina (Support): Can you paste the events? even small snippets help.

maria (Customer Success): From their kube events: ```Warning  FailedAttach  2m  attach-controller  attach failed: timeout waiting for attach``` and our attach-retry in the platform shows repeated auth 403 for the service account during the same window.

dom (SRE): Important: this might be a combined symptom. 403 on attach + probe failures -> autoscaler interprets pods as unready -> won't count for headroom. Check probe rate limits and attach auth rotation.

kevin (Platform): I'm looking at the tenant logs for BrightCart. I see attach auth rotation happened 08:10:52 -> rotation succeeded -> then at 08:11:05 several imagepull backoffs from noisy-tenant-445. However the autoscaler didn't request more nodes because minReplica floor = 4 and desired = 4 at that moment.

lina (Support): So they were stuck at minReplica, but we expected warm chain to add ephemeral pods. Any throttles?

kevin (Platform): There are probe-suppression signals: our probe gateway returned 429s for health checks during the peak for about 45s. That would prevent readiness gates flipping. Snip from platform logs: ```PROBE_GATEWAY request_id=abcd status=429 reason=rate_limit source=10.3.2.14```

dom (SRE): That lines up. If probes are rate-limited, pods stay NotReady, autoscaler won't scale because it sees no capacity delta (we avoid scaling if many pods are unready to prevent thundering). Also check noisy neighbor: I see one node with high CPU (noisy-tenant-445) causing kube-scheduler delays.

maria (Customer Success): Customer: "We never hit CPU on our app, it's all queueing and 429s" — they don't have noisy workloads. Could be platform-level noisy tenant.

lina (Support): Quick repro steps we asked the customer to run: 1) curl their endpoint with burst at lower QPS to reproduce 429s; 2) upload the diagnostics bundle. They sent bundle id bc-2026-03-17-08.

dom (SRE): I pulled the diagnostics. Important lines: ```autoscaler decision: desired_replicas=8 reason=scale_up_allowed headroom=0 unready_pods=3``` and then later ```scaleup suppressed: insufficient_ready_count```. So autoscaler wanted to scale but suppressed due to readiness heuristics.

kevin (Platform): Another signal: registry pulls got transient 403 during rotation window for some images. That caused pod init delays ~20-30s each which kept them NotReady longer. Combined with probe rate limits, it snowballed.

lina (Support): TL;DR chain: auth rotation momentarily affected imagepulls/attach -> pod init/readiness delayed -> probes rate-limited -> autoscaler suppressed scaling -> customer saw 429s.

maria (Customer Success): Customer wants a mitigation and root cause. They asked why the dedicated pool didn't scale faster.

dom (SRE): Immediate mitigations we can offer: 1) temporarily raise minReplicas or reserved burst for that tenant; 2) relax readiness suppression threshold for short windows (careful with thundering); 3) increase probe gateway quota for critical tenants.

kevin (Platform): For root cause: investigate service account rotation logic that produced 403s for registry/attach for ~45s. Also review probe gateway rate limiting and consider token prioritization for attach/imagepull requests from Dedicated nodes.

lina (Support): I'll propose a mitigation plan to BrightCart: a) apply a one-off burst reservation to get them instant headroom b) set up a canary policy to avoid suppression for next weekdays morning ramp c) open a follow-up with Platform to share findings.

autoscale-bot: Incident guardrail triggered: suppressed-scaleup-not-ready threshold hit for tenant BrightCart at 08:11:15 (count=3) :warning:

maria (Customer Success): Customer accepted the burst reservation for now, asking for ETA on a permanent fix.

dom (SRE): Next steps for us: - Platform to surface attach/imagepull auth logs correlated with KMS rotations - Dev infra to examine probe gateway rate limits and soft quotas - Product to review unsafe relaxation of readiness suppression. I'll own timeline and follow-up.

kevin (Platform): I'll attach the auth log snippet and a query to find other tenants affected in the same window. Query: ```index=platform_logs service=attach status=403 | stats count by tenant, status```

lina (Support): Thanks all. I'll keep the thread updated with the customer's response. :thumbsup:
